Latent heat flux as the residual of the surface energy balance

Source: R/metric-latent-heat.R
ef_latent_heat.Rd

Computes the instantaneous latent heat flux \(LE\) at the land surface as the residual of the surface energy balance: the net radiation minus the soil heat flux and the sensible heat flux. This is how the METRIC model obtains the energy used for evapotranspiration at the satellite overpass time.

Usage

ef_latent_heat(rn, g, h)

Arguments

rn

Numeric. Instantaneous net radiation \(R_n\) [W m-2], for example from ef_net_radiation(). Positive when it supplies energy to the surface. Any finite value.

g

Numeric. Instantaneous soil heat flux \(G\) [W m-2], positive when heat flows from the surface into the soil. Any finite value.

h

Numeric. Instantaneous sensible heat flux \(H\) [W m-2], positive when heat flows from the surface into the air. Any finite value.

Value

A numeric vector of latent heat flux \(LE\) [W m-2] with the common length of the inputs, positive when the surface loses energy by evaporation. If the inputs include matrices or arrays (all with the same dim), the result keeps that dim. Negative values are returned unchanged (see Details).

Details

The surface energy balance (FAO-56, chapter 1, Eq. 1) is \(R_n - G - \lambda ET - H = 0\), where \(\lambda ET\) is the latent heat flux. Solved for the latent heat flux, $$LE = R_n - G - H$$ with the FAO-56 sign convention: positive \(R_n\) supplies energy to the surface, and positive \(G\), \(LE\) and \(H\) remove energy from it.

Assumptions (FAO-56, chapter 1): only vertical fluxes are considered (horizontal advection is ignored), the surface is extensive and homogeneous, and heat storage in the canopy and metabolic energy are neglected. These assumptions are weaker in mixed pixels of about 1 km. Because \(LE\) is a residual, the balance closes by construction in every pixel and all the errors of \(R_n\), \(G\) and \(H\) are transferred to \(LE\).

Negative values are physically possible inputs: \(R_n\), \(G\) and \(H\) may all be negative, and no sign check is made. A negative \(LE\) (\(H > R_n - G\)) is returned unchanged and without a warning; it is never set to zero. It is flagged downstream with EF_ET_NEGATIVE on the evapotranspiration layers (\(LE < 0\) is equivalent to \(ET_{inst} < 0\)). An \(LE\) larger than \(R_n - G\) (negative \(H\), possible under advection) is not modified either.

The function is symmetric in g and h: swapping them gives the same result. Use named arguments.

Missing values (NA, NaN) in any input propagate to the corresponding output element, without errors or warnings. Arguments must be numeric (double or integer) and have length 1 or a common length; length-1 arguments are recycled, arrays with a dim are not. Infinite values raise an error of class earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error) that names the argument.

Verification status: VERIFICADA as the FAO-56 surface energy balance (chapter 1, Eq. 1, rearranged). Its use as a residual in METRIC is corroborated by secondary sources (Olmedo et al., 2016, Eq. 1); the equation number in Allen et al. (2007) has not been verified.

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

Olmedo, G. F., Ortega-Farias, S., de la Fuente-Saiz, D., Fonseca-Luengo, D., & Fuentes-Penailillo, F. (2016). water: Tools and functions to estimate actual evapotranspiration using land surface energy balance models in R. The R Journal, 8(2), 352-369. doi:10.32614/RJ-2016-051

See also

Other latent heat and evapotranspiration functions: ef_et_daily(), ef_et_inst(), ef_etrf()

Examples

# Reference case: 600 - 60 - 50 = 490 W m-2
ef_latent_heat(rn = 600, g = 60, h = 50)
#> [1] 490

# H larger than the available energy: LE is negative and kept
ef_latent_heat(rn = 400, g = 80, h = 369)
#> [1] -49

# Several pixels sharing one soil heat flux value (recycled)
ef_latent_heat(rn = c(550, 600, 620), g = 60, h = c(40, 50, 300))
#> [1] 450 490 260
